sections.label: New stamp duty for PHEs
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new stamp duty treatment for acquiring and disposing equity interests in property holding entities, effective on or after 11 March 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a new stamp duty treatment for the acquisition and disposal of equity interests in property holding entities (PHEs).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This new stamp duty treatment addresses the stamp duty rate differential that presently exists between the direct acquisition or disposal of residential properties and the acquisition or disposal of equity interests in entities whose primary tangible assets are residential properties in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This Bill, if approved by Parliament, will take effect on or after 11 March 2017.

sections.label: Additional Conveyance Duties on PHE equity
sections.summary: The Bill applies Additional Conveyance Duties to acquisition and disposal of equity interest in entities whose primary tangible assets are Singapore residential properties, regardless of bona fide business reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Bill thus seeks to apply new duties to the acquisition and disposal of equity interest in entities whose primary tangible assets are in residential properties in Singapore under specified circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These new duties, which I henceforth refer to as Additional Conveyance Duties (ACD), will apply irrespective of whether the equity interest in PHEs is acquired or disposed of for bona fide business reasons.

sections.label: Definition of property holding entity
sections.summary: An entity can be a PHE if 50% or more of its total tangible assets is residential properties in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: An entity can be a PHE if 50% or more of its total tangible assets is residential properties in Singapore.

sections.label: ACD for significant owner buyers
sections.summary: Acquisition of equity interest in a PHE is subject to ACD for a buyer who is or becomes a significant owner, at 1% to 3% and a flat 15%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With the new measure, an acquisition of equity interest in a PHE will be subject to ACD for the buyer, if the buyer is already a significant owner at the time of acquisition, or becomes a significant owner thereafter.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, 1% to 3% on the value of the underlying residential properties which mirrors the existing BSD.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, a flat 15% on the value of the underlying residential properties, which is similar to the existing ABSD for residential properties.

sections.label: ACD flat rate for early sale
sections.summary: ACD is set at a flat rate of 12% for sale of equity interest within three years of purchase, similar to SSD for residential properties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: ACD will be set at a flat rate of 12% for sale of equity interest within three years of purchase, similar to SSD for residential properties.

sections.label: Reviewing ownership for residential properties
sections.summary: The speaker raised reviewing ownership of residential properties to include beneficial interests, proposing normal residential stamp duties apply when shares of a company holding such property are transferred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I brought up this issue during the Budget Debate last Wednesday, asking that we review the concept of ownership for residential properties to include beneficial interests instead of just looking at the registered owner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I had proposed that if a residential property is held by a corporate entity or a special purpose vehicle, and the shares of the company are transferred from seller to buyer, the normal residential stamp duties should apply.

sections.label: Bill motivation not revenue
sections.summary: The measures were studied carefully and the Bill's motivation is not to raise revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we have been studying this very carefully before working out the measures that have been proposed today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I should also clarify that the motivation for this Bill is not to raise revenue.

sections.label: Anti-avoidance provision for new duties
sections.summary: A specific anti-avoidance provision covers arrangements reducing or avoiding liability of the new duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Indeed, we have also put in place, as I mentioned in my Second Reading speech just now, a specific anti-avoidance provision for the new measure, which will have the ability to cover arrangements that have the effect of reducing or avoiding liability of the new duties.

sections.label: Three Sittings market sensitivity
sections.summary: Measures were studied carefully and taken in three Sittings due to market sensitivity, not to rush.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we took time to study, to carefully consider the measures before putting it together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are doing it three Sittings in one, not to rush through but because of the market sensitivity of the measure.

sections.label: PHE prevalence and share transfer exemptions
sections.summary: Prevalence of PHE practice is unknown as those transferring shares need not declare; exemptions for parent-child and death transfers are questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In other words, how prevalent is this PHE practice and would this Bill result in sudden movements in the market?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We would not know how prevalent it is because the people who are doing this today, doing this share transfer, are not required to declare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would not want to speculate on the impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We know that there is a differential which we are closing today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the case of, let us say, the parents transferring the share to their children, and also transferring due to death of the shareholders, and so transfer to the beneficiaries, would that also be exempted?
